about: Reviewed decisions applied by convert.js. Each entry carries its reason, so the page's data can be rebuilt and audited.
heatwaveReason: Events about the same heatwave as a record on /heatwaves/ link to it; that record is then not repeated as its own marker on the timeline.

countdown-2018.what: The Lancet Countdown reported heat exposure and labour-capacity indicators in its annual framework, including a heat-related labour-loss estimate.
countdown-2018.reason: Its only source could not be read by the checks (a robot wall), so the figure it carried is left out and the general point kept. Removed: 41 indicators.

globalforum-2018.what: The forum had a Southeast Asian regional focus and attention to communication. Its description distinguishes the formal launch from earlier founding.
globalforum-2018.reason: Its only source could not be read by the checks (a robot wall), so the figure it carried is left out and the general point kept. Removed: 17 to 20 December.

northwest-2021.what: CDC reported a sharp rise in heat-related emergency-department visits in its northwestern surveillance region during the late-June heatwave, and highlighted near-real-time surveillance for guiding response.
northwest-2021.reason: Its only source could not be read by the checks (a robot wall), so the figure it carried is left out and the general point kept. Removed: 2,779 visits, June 25-30.

researchgrowth-2021.what: A review of Web of Science papers reported rapid growth in heatwave research, with prominent attention to events in 1995 and 2003.
researchgrowth-2021.reason: Its only source could not be read by the checks (a robot wall), so the figure it carried is left out and the general point kept. Removed: 8,011 papers, doubling within about 5 years.

the-transition-remains-uneven-and-incomp.text: A regional history of media attention was not verified here. Disaster databases and epidemiological mortality estimates count different things. Country coverage in this review is uneven, and absence from this timeline is not evidence of inaction.
the-transition-remains-uneven-and-incomp.reason: The bibliometric review behind "scientific publication growth is measurable" (S26) could not be confirmed or archived, so that clause is left out.

Media and public attention.text: No comparable, reproducible South and Southeast Asian media series, Google Trends extract or multilingual coverage study was opened and verified. A study of research publications could not be confirmed either. No media-attention peak is dated here.
Media and public attention.reason: Its reference to a verified bibliometric study (S26) no longer holds: that source could not be confirmed or archived.
